subject: Digitisation/quote enquiry: seven items, Western Manuscripts and Blenheim Papers
body:
Dear Imaging Services,

I am asking on behalf of a small non-commercial project that reads cipher passages in digitised historical letters. One person directs the project and sends every message; the reading of images, the searches of editions and the checks are done by AI agents (Claude models) working in a public repository where every step is logged.

None of the following is currently digitised online. Could you quote for digital reproductions, and let me know whether each needs an in-person Reader Pass visit instead (I understand the Library cannot scan an original manuscript without an existing microfilm surrogate)?

1. Add MS 21483, ff.1-8 (anonymous 1669 cipher letters with a partial key to names)
2. Add MS 8693 (first volume of Add MS 8693-8698, Sacchetti's cipher despatch registers, 1624-26) -- please also say whether your internal folio-level description marks any leaves "cipher"/"cypher," before I consider the other five volumes
3. Add MS 20318-20319 (Gualterio Papers, 1700) -- please also say whether your description of this pair notes "decipherings" the way it does for the related Add MS 20244
4. Add MS 18982, ff.95r-96v (a 1645 letter with its own contemporary decipherment)
5. Add MS 61137, ff.41 and 55 (Blenheim Papers, Raby-Hedges 1704 correspondence)
6. Harley MS 287, ff.39-40, f.11, ff.70r-72v (three already partly-read 1587-88 items; this is for finishing images, not a fresh attempt)
7. Add MS 32093, f.423 (a letter partly in cipher relating to General Monck, 1659-60, catalogued "Imperfect" -- could you also say what "Imperfect" refers to: damage, a missing portion, or a loose leaf?)

I am not committing to any payment at this stage; I would just like the quotes and to know which items need a reading-room visit. Any reading we obtain will be published under an open licence, naming the item and shelfmark, at https://github.com/NoAutopilot/cipher-lab

With thanks,

[SIGN-OFF]
